BaselineCodingRules.keywords: baseline, language_agnostic, contracts, error_handling, naming, yagni, ai_to_ai

BeliefState.Axiom: A name states a goal, not a pattern. Forbidden semantic-noise names: `Manager`, `Handler`, `Data`, `Info`, `Wrapper`, `Util`, `do…`, `process…`. `OrderFulfillmentPipeline` carries intent; `OrderManager` tells the next reader nothing. Use precise verbs (`retrieve`, `verify`, `compose`) over vague ones (`get`, `check`, `make`).

Failures are explicit and carry cause. Raise/return a specific, typed error with a message that says what failed and with what input; when re-raising, preserve the original cause (do not flatten a stack into a string). Never silently swallow an error or return a zero value that hides one.

The public surface documents its contract: inputs, output, and failure modes, at the declaration — not buried in the body. A caller must be able to use the function from its signature plus one doc block, without reading the implementation.
Comments carry intent the code cannot: purpose, invariant, side effect, failure mode, non-goal, or why-not. A comment that restates the syntax on the next line is noise and must be removed.

Build only what the task needs. No speculative abstraction (an interface/base class for a single caller with no confirmed second one), no dead code, and no defensive branches against states the types or invariants already exclude. Prefer the simplest shape that satisfies the contract.
A unit does one thing at one level of abstraction. A function that mixes I/O, policy, and formatting is split. Depth of nesting and length are symptoms; name the extracted piece by its goal.

AntiPattern.Bad: A caught error that is logged-and-ignored, discarded, or replaced by a generic message that drops the original cause — so the failure surfaces later with no trace of its origin.
AntiPattern.Instead: Handle it (recover with a documented fallback) or propagate it with the cause attached. One or the other, never neither.

AntiPattern.Bad: `FooManager`, `DataHandler`, `RequestWrapper`, `doWork`, `processItem` — names that describe a code pattern rather than a business goal.
`// increment i` above `i++`; a doc block that repeats parameter names and types already in the signature.
AntiPattern.Instead: Comment the why, the invariant, or the non-obvious consequence — or nothing.

AntiPattern.Bad: Extracting an interface, factory, or config option for one caller "in case we need it".
AntiPattern.Instead: Inline it; abstract on the second real consumer, when the variance is known.

Hook.Purpose: The scope's own quality gate (formatter + linter + type/compile check + tests, as the project declares them) passes on the changed files.
Hook.Expected: Exit 0. If the scope has not declared its gate yet, that is the finding to fix first.

Hook.Purpose: No placeholder/scaffold markers survive in shipped code.
Hook.Expected: Empty on changed lines; a real deferred item belongs in a ticket, not a bare marker.

BaselineCodingRules.RewardCriteria: ✅ Names state a goal; precise verbs; no `Manager`/`Handler`/`Data`/`Util`/`do…`/`process…`. ✅ Every failure path raises/returns a specific error with context and preserved cause. ✅ Public entities document inputs, output, and failure modes at the declaration. ✅ Comments carry intent (purpose / invariant / side effect / failure / non-goal), never restate syntax. ✅ Only what the task needs: no speculative abstraction, no dead code, no defense against impossible states. ✅ Each unit has one responsibility at one abstraction level. ❌ An error caught and dropped, or re-raised with the cause lost. ❌ Pattern-shaped names that hide the business goal. ❌ Comments that restate the code, or doc blocks duplicating the signature. ❌ An abstraction introduced for a single caller with no confirmed second consumer. ❌ Placeholder/scaffold markers (`TODO`, `<NAME>`) left in shipped code.
